rationale: Acceptance skipped (no-spec, no ArtifactRef); confidence capped at low. Four patch findings: double-logging in local mode before re-raise (CR-001), `raise e` resets traceback to handler instead of original exception site (CR-002), `request_id: null` key emitted in non-local 500 JSON when uuid is absent (CR-003, reachability uncertain), and missing Apache 2.0 license header in the new test file that will fail the `make license-check` gate (CR-004, standards). One deferred: CORS headers absent on local re-raised exceptions (pre-existing middleware ordering, not introduced by this change; see code-review-deferred.md). Six candidates dismissed as false positives after source verification.

standards_review.notes: Single commit 'EPMCDME-14713: Remove traceback disclosure from global exception middleware' matches the documented EPMCDME-####: Description format exactly.

New file tests/codemie/rest_api/test_handle_exceptions.py has no Apache 2.0 license header. The guide requires all new source files to carry the header; tests/conftest.py (modified in the same change) and all other test files in the repo carry it. The new file starts directly with 'from __future__ import annotations'.

The change removes traceback disclosure from the HTTP 500 response body, replacing it with a generic message plus a request_id correlation token. The full traceback is retained in server logs via logger.error(e, exc_info=True), which is correct. No credentials are logged, no untrusted input normalization introduced, and no auth/authz regressions. The change is a net security improvement.

findings.title: Logger fires before local re-raise, causing double-log
findings.problem: `logger.error(e, exc_info=True)` at line 1082 runs unconditionally before the `if config.is_local: raise e` branch. In local mode the exception is re-raised after logging, and the ASGI server (uvicorn) logs the propagated exception a second time.
findings.impact: Local development logs contain duplicate error entries for every unhandled exception, adding noise and potentially confusing developers correlating logs to a request.
findings.recommendation: Move `logger.error` inside the non-local branch only: `if config.is_local: raise` (bare) `else: logger.error(e, exc_info=True); return JSONResponse(...)`. This eliminates the double-log and also fixes CR-002 at the same time.

findings.title: `raise e` resets traceback to handler line
findings.problem: Line 1085 uses `raise e` instead of bare `raise`. Python's `raise <expr>` form resets the traceback to the `raise` statement itself, discarding the original call chain.
findings.impact: In local mode the printed traceback ends at `main.py:1085` rather than the actual exception origin; developers must infer where the exception was originally raised, defeating the purpose of the local re-raise path.
findings.recommendation: Replace `raise e` with bare `raise` to preserve the full original traceback chain.

findings.title: Null `request_id` key emitted in 500 JSON when uuid absent
findings.problem: `request_id = getattr(request.state, 'uuid', None)` can be `None` if `configure_logging` threw before setting `request.state.uuid`, or if the middleware stack is reconfigured. The value is included in the response unconditionally as `"request_id": null`. Reachability is uncertain given current middleware ordering (configure_logging reliably sets uuid before handle_exceptions can catch an exception), but the null key is still emitted when the edge case fires.
findings.impact: Clients that rely on `request_id` presence for correlation receive `null`, which is indistinguishable from an intentionally absent key and leaks that the tracing middleware did not run.
findings.recommendation: Generate a fallback UUID when uuid is absent: `request_id = getattr(request.state, 'uuid', None) or str(uuid.uuid4())`, or conditionally omit the key: include `'request_id': request_id` in `content` only when `request_id` is not `None`.

findings.title: Missing Apache 2.0 license header in new test file
findings.problem: The new file begins directly with `from __future__ import annotations` with no copyright/license block. The code-quality guide requires all new source files to carry the Apache 2.0 header; every other test file in the repo, including the modified `tests/conftest.py`, carries it.
findings.impact: The `make license-check` gate will fail on this file, blocking the pipeline.
findings.recommendation: Prepend the Apache 2.0 header block used in `tests/conftest.py` (lines 1-13) to the top of `tests/codemie/rest_api/test_handle_exceptions.py`, then verify with `make license-check`.
